01 / Orientation

Start with the central question

Use a short opening to orient the reader before introducing detail. Keep paragraphs focused, define unfamiliar terms, and use headings that tell the reader what each section contributes.

02 / The main idea

Make the important point easy to find

Reserve callouts for ideas that deserve a pause—not for every paragraph. A callout should clarify or summarize the surrounding explanation.

Key idea

A useful takeaway is brief enough to scan and specific enough to remember.

03 / Supporting detail

Use structure when it improves understanding

Choose a table for comparisons, a diagram for relationships, and a list for steps. Avoid turning ordinary paragraphs into cards just for decoration.

// Keep examples short and relevant
const idea = "clarity before decoration";
